question.problem:
Consider the vector-valued function $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{4}$ defined by

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 \\ 4 & 5 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}]x.
$$

 

What is $\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x},$ the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x$ at ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a vector-valued function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ with respect to a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ is the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋱ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{m\times n}.
$$

In our case, writing out the function $f(x)$ where $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{2}$, we get

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 \\ 4 & 5 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} \\ 6{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

So, the total derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{4}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{4}}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(4{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(4{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(6{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(6{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 \\ 4 & 5 \\ 6 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Since the total derivative is a constant matrix, evaluating it at ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ gives the same matrix.
